$notes.gpt-image-2 idea: The single row it trips is site/mark, and site/mark is the company's own primary mark — the one asset in this repository every other surface is a member of the family of. plan.ts asks for 'a low ash ridge — one flat baseline with a single shallow arc rising from it, like the face of an anvil seen from the front — and one solid ember flame rising above the centre of that arc. Two elements only.' What came back is one curved bar (the baseline and the arc collapsed into a single element) under a solid chamfered octagon with a short spike on its top edge. The octagon is not a flame and does not read as one at any size. Every other clause is honoured — flat fill, one accent, near-black ground, nothing drawn in white or grey — which is precisely why this is a criterion-1 failure that criterion 1's MEASUREMENTS all pass.
$notes.gpt-image-2 lettering: All nine names set correctly: Forge Create, Developer Platform, Forge Foresight, Forge Hub, Forge Market, Forge Network, CloudsForge, Forge Trade, Forge Worlds. That includes hub, where the reference set's own row records FLUX inventing 'Home on the Ridge' out of the idea text. This is the second challenger in a row to beat FLUX cleanly on lettering and the first to beat it while also keeping the accent: the letterforms are set in the surface accent on eight of the nine, developers/wordmark being the exception at plain white. Tracking is very wide on all nine — a house style of the model rather than a defect the rubric names — and the mark component is drawn noticeably smaller relative to the lettering than the reference sets it.
$notes.gpt-image-2 ground, and why the row is a: On review/compare/compare-mark.png the gpt-image-2 grounds visibly band and streak where the reference grounds are dead flat, and it would be easy to score 'ground not the brand near-black' as a 12. Measured, the border band of the twelve reference marks holds exactly ONE colour each, and the twelve gpt-image-2 marks hold 82 to 125 (median 101). But the reference figure is an artefact of normalise_ground.py having snapped those files after generation, not of FLUX having drawn them flat: the only two reference files that were never normalised measure 214 and 232 unique colours in the same band (COMPARISON.md section 11.2). Raw against raw, gpt-image-2's ground is roughly twice as flat as FLUX's and is the correct hue family, so the row is a 0 on the merits. What the sheet is showing is one set that has been through the normaliser next to one that has not.
$notes.gpt-image-2, and what these eight rows c: This column reads 0,0,0,0,0,0,1,0 against the reference's 0,0,0,0,0,0,0,1 — two nearly clean columns tripping one row each, and different rows. That is a true tally and it is close to useless as a verdict, which is worth recording rather than hiding. The taxonomy was fixed in COMPARISON.md section 4 to catch what the previous challenger did (Qwen: 6 guides, 5 frames, 6 non-flat, 3 pale grounds, 5 missing accents), and gpt-image-2 does none of those things — it is the most literally compliant set this repository has generated. It has no row for 'drew every clause and still produced something nobody reads as fire', which is the actual finding of section 11.3, and no row for 'the mark and the favicon of the same surface do not read as the same idea', which is where site actually falls down. That last one was nearly written here as a gpt-image-2 defect and is not one on its own: laid side by side at /tmp, the REFERENCE site/mark and site/favicon are not the same drawing either — the mark is an orange arc on a flat bar, the favicon a bone arch with no bar and a fuller flame. Both models redraw rather than reuse, because each asset is a separate generation from a separate prompt and nothing in the pipeline asks for consistency between them. The difference is that FLUX's two both read as a fire over an arch, so the family survives the redraw, while gpt-image-2's favicon is a tall organic flame and its mark is an octagon, so it does not. Read the rows for what they measure and take the verdict from section 11.5.
$notes.qwen-image-2512-positive has no column h: That set holds two assets — currency-ember/mark and currency-spark/mark — and every column above is counted out of 12 marks and 9 wordmarks. $pilot.$scope: This repository's contribution to the estate-wide 15-asset positive-dialect pilot, COMPARISON.md section 9.3. TWO assets — currency-ember/mark and currency-spark/mark — so every figure below is out of 2, not out of the 12 and 9 the columns above use. The other 13 are emberkin's 9 `types` icons and aetherholm's 4 `icons/resource-*`, each recorded in that repository's own $pilot block. claims.py sums the three and checks the section 9.3 table against the sum, which is how a row that does not add up is caught: the table shipped `idea not recognisable` at 2 of 15 for the literal column when the three contributions sum to 1, and the prose four paragraphs below it said 1.
